h: Where it fits on the Eastern Esplanade
p: Funtopia is on Eastern Esplanade, the stretch of seafront that runs east from the pier towards Thorpe Bay. It's a slightly calmer side of Southend than the area right around the pier, and close to the old Kursaal, the town's historic amusement hall with its distinctive dome, which is a landmark in its own right.

A couple of tips for making indoor play run smoothly. Pack socks for everyone, because they're almost always needed at play centres, and a drink bottle each so little ones stay topped up after charging about. It can get warm indoors, so layers you can peel off are better than one big coat.

Timing makes a big difference too. Rainy days and school holidays are when everybody has the same idea, so arriving earlier in the day is usually the way to get the most out of it before it gets busy. On a sunny day, it can be a lot quieter, which is great if you've got younger kids who don't love crowds.

After you're done, the seafront walk is right there. Head east and you'll find quieter stretches of beach towards Thorpe Bay, or turn west for the pier and the brighter lights of the main seafront. Southend has no shortage of chippies, cafés and ice cream kiosks to refuel along the way.
For a full weekend, Old Leigh is a short trip west along the coast and has a completely different feel, with cockle sheds and fishing boats in the creek.
